1.explanation:
• audits/critical-request-chains.js: This is the audit that traverses the dependency tree and flags any high-priority resources as part of the “critical request chain.” It is where the final list of critical chains is built and displayed. It needs to be updated so that rel=preload (as=style) CSS does not count as a blocking resource.

• lib/dependency-graph/network-node.js: The hasRenderBlockingPriority() method here classifies network requests as “render-blocking” based solely on DevTools priority (e.g. ‘High’ or ‘VeryHigh’). Because preload-as-style inherits a high priority, it’s currently treated as blocking. Adjusting this logic (for example, by detecting rel=preload or as=style) will prevent CSS preloads from showing up as critical.

• gather/computed/page-dependency-graph.js: This builds the network/CPU dependency graph used by the audit. Although it doesn’t itself filter based on priority, it is the source of the tree that critical-request-chains traverses. If preload nodes should be pruned entirely, this is where they would be excluded from the graph before the audit runs.
1.bug_scenario: On page load, a stylesheet is fetched via a <link rel="preload" as="style" onload="this.rel='stylesheet'"> tag and deliberately delayed by 5 seconds on the server. In Lighthouse’s Performance > Diagnostics › Critical Request Chains panel, the CSS preload request (slow.css) appears in the “critical request chain,” showing a ~5 s blocking chain—even though rel=preload should load resources without blocking initial rendering.
